title: On Compact Topological Spaces and Fixed Point Theorems
abstract: We investigate compact topological spaces and prove several fixed point theorems using auxiliary lemmas.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction and Preliminaries
sections.text:
In this paper we review topological spaces.
Definition 1.1. A topological space X is compact if every open cover has a finite subcover.
Example 1. The unit sphere S^n is a compact manifold.
Remark 1. Compactness is preserved under continuous maps.

sections.heading: 2. Main Results
sections.text:
We present the main lemmas and theorems.
Lemma 2.1. Closed subsets of compact spaces are compact.
Theorem 3.2. Theorem 3.2 follows from Lemma 2.1. Every continuous map f on a compact metric space has a fixed point.
Proof of Theorem 3.2. Apply Lemma 2.1 and Definition 1.1 directly.
Corollary 3.3. By Theorem 3.2, closed bounded sets in R^n have fixed points.
We extend Theorem 3.2 to non-metric spaces.
